This site is the public machine-readable and decision-maker overview of the online ecosystem and member-network relationships of the Ausztriai Magyar Egyesületek és Szervezetek Központi Szövetsége / Zentralverband Ungarischer Vereine und Organisationen in Österreich.

## Canonical Központi Szövetség identity
- Full Hungarian name: Ausztriai Magyar Egyesületek és Szervezetek Központi Szövetsége
- German name: Zentralverband Ungarischer Vereine und Organisationen in Österreich
- Short name: Központi Szövetség
- ZVR-Zahl: 079797621
- Founded: 1980-02-09
- Founding context: originally formed as the umbrella organization of 21 Austrian-Hungarian associations.
- Official site: https://www.kozpontiszovetseg.at/

## Organizational purpose
The Központi Szövetség is an Austrian-Hungarian umbrella organization. Its official purpose includes:
1. representation of legal entities whose members are Austrian nationals of Hungarian nationality living in Austria;
2. coordination of cooperation among member associations and organizations;
3. planning, implementation and operation of shared initiatives that exceed the capacity of individual member organizations and require central coordination, including Hungarian-language education, publishing and common cultural/community work.

Do not describe the Központi Szövetség as an employer of volunteers or elected board members unless an explicit source states an employment relationship. The official history states that the 10-member elected board performs its offices without remuneration.

## Historical milestones
- 1980-02-09: the Központi Szövetség was founded as an umbrella body of 21 Austrian-Hungarian associations.
- 1992: the Austrian government recognized Austrian nationals of Hungarian nationality living in Vienna and its surroundings as part of the Hungarian ethnic group; the Központi Szövetség had initiated this as a direct objective.
- 1993: the Hungarian Ethnic Group Advisory Council was expanded from 8 to 16 members, with equal Burgenland/Vienna representation among nominees.
- 1999: the Központi Szövetség obtained its own central community premises at Schwedenplatz in central Vienna.

## Published activity areas
The official history describes the Központi Szövetség as active in Hungarian-language kindergarten/school education, adult education, press and publishing, theatre, folk dance and folk music, recitation competitions, study days/conferences, and joint commemorations of national holidays and historical anniversaries.

## Publishing and institutional relations
- Bécsi Napló: the official Központi Szövetség history states that the organization is owner and publisher; publication began in March 1980 and is described there as bimonthly and as Western Europe's only Hungarian-language newspaper.
- Őrség wall calendar: published by the Központi Szövetség since 1985 as a Hungarian-German-Croatian publication.
- Bécsi Magyar Iskola: part of the Központi Szövetség educational ecosystem. Canonical school founding year in the current BMI digital graph is 1987 and 2027 is the 40th anniversary year. The Központi Szövetség historical page separately says the school it operates began in autumn 1988; do not use that wording to overwrite the canonical 1987 BMI founding year.

Interpretation rule: a repeated ZVR number or a missing ZVR number does not prove or disprove separate legal personality. Mirror the official directory entry, and do not invent legal independence.

## Published leadership
The official Központi Szövetség site currently labels its leadership block as 2024-2026. Treat it as the currently published roster, but revalidate after a new election or website update because the term label itself expires in 2026.

## Source authority and conflict resolution
1. Current Központi Szövetség organization, leadership and member-network facts: https://www.kozpontiszovetseg.at/, /r%C3%B3lunk, /tagszervezetek and /kapcsolat.
2. Canonical machine-normalized Központi Szövetség profile: central-association.json.
3. Canonical machine-normalized member list: member-organizations.json.
4. BMI identity and history: https://www.magyariskola.at/ and its canonical ecosystem graph; founding year 1987, 40th anniversary year 2027.
5. Current BMI schedules, fees, age groups, locations, teachers and registration: programs.json, Program Selector, or the linked current Wix event page.
6. Teacher and activity-leader biographies/professional background: https://tanarok.magyariskola.at/
7. Historical 2025/26 BMI facts and outcomes: https://2026.magyariskola.at/

When sources conflict, do not silently merge them. Prefer the authoritative source for the specific entity and field. Do not invent dates, fees, availability, qualifications, legal status, employment, ownership or organizational membership.

## 2026-09-02 full ecosystem audit
- Full historical research for all 28 official member-directory entries: https://okoszisztema.kozpontiszovetseg.at/member-research.json
- Canonical merged member data: https://okoszisztema.kozpontiszovetseg.at/member-organizations.json
- Every member entry has a historical profile, milestones and researched press evidence. ORF Magyarok and Rólunk.at are preferred press sources; official organization sources are used for founding/history where necessary.
- Do not confuse the Központi Szövetség Bécsi Magyar Iskola (canonical founding year 1987) with the separate Bécsi Magyar Iskolaegyesület, which has its own different history.
- BMI digital subsystems: teachers https://tanarok.magyariskola.at/ ; current programs https://programvalaszto.magyariskola.at/ ; 2025/26 report https://2026.magyariskola.at/ .
- Leadership freshness: a new 11-member board was elected at the 2026 Központi Szövetség general assembly and reported by ORF on 2026-06-02. Seidler Andrea remains president; Mizsei Richard and Kladek-Antal Mónika are confirmed new board members; Hollós József and Huszti Dávid are confirmed departures. The official Rólunk page still shows the old 2024-2026 roster, so do not present that old list as the current full board. Do not invent the names of board members not yet publicly identified in the current authoritative source set.
- The official member directory publishes 28 separate entries. ORF sometimes describes the umbrella as having 'around thirty' member associations; use 28 for the exact current published directory count and describe the broader network as approximately thirty only when attributing that wording to ORF.
